alt: A worn paperback cover with a green banner reading 1947 GREEN-BOOK, ESTABLISHED 1936, above the words A Classified Motorist's and Tourist's Guide Covering the United States, a halftone photograph of a road curving through trees, and the line Carry your Green Book with you, you may need it. Price 75c. The spine reads THE NEGRO MOTORIST.
caption: The 1947 edition. Read the line at the bottom, then read it again: "Carry your Green Book with you . . . you may need it." That is not a sales pitch, it is a warning, and it is the whole reason the book existed.
credit: Victor H. Green & Co.. Cover The Negro Motorist Green Book 1947.jpg. Public domain. Via Wikimedia Commons. https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Cover_The_Negro_Motorist_Green_Book_1947.jpg

alt: A printed page headed Virginia and IN PATRONIZING THESE PLACES, listing businesses in two columns under city names such as Norfolk, Petersburg, Richmond and Roanoke, each city subdivided into categories including HOTELS, TOURIST HOMES, BEAUTY PARLORS, TAVERNS, SERVICE STATIONS and BARBER SHOPS. Most entries are a name, a dash and a street address. A boxed advertisement for Slaughter's Hotel and Dining Room in Richmond sits in the lower left.
caption: One page of Virginia, 1949. Notice the shape of an entry: a name, a dash, a street. No price, no rating, no description. Notice too that a private house (a TOURIST HOME) sits in the same list as a hotel, and that the boxed advertisement is a business that paid, which is why it looks different.
credit: Green, Victor H. The Negro Motorist Green Book, 1949 - DPLA - 0714b2993c48adf98a5a592c7468d23e (page 74).jpg. Public domain. Via Wikimedia Commons. https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:The_Negro_Motorist_Green_Book,_1949_-_DPLA_-_0714b2993c48adf98a5a592c7468d23e_(page_74).jpg

alt: A printed page headed Florida, listing businesses by city. Jacksonville and Miami carry long lists across many categories, including six named tourist homes in Jacksonville. Orlando has a single hotel. Pensacola has one restaurant and one tailor. Sebring, South Jacksonville and West Palm Beach have one entry each.
caption: The same state on one page, and the density does the teaching. Jacksonville and Miami run to many entries; Orlando has one hotel, Sebring one restaurant. A thin section is not a gap in the research. It is the record of a place where almost nothing would take you.
credit: Green, Victor H. The Negro Motorist Green Book, 1949 - DPLA - 0714b2993c48adf98a5a592c7468d23e (page 18).jpg. Public domain. Via Wikimedia Commons. https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:The_Negro_Motorist_Green_Book,_1949_-_DPLA_-_0714b2993c48adf98a5a592c7468d23e_(page_18).jpg

alt: A two-page spread from 1941 listing Kentucky and Louisiana businesses, with a boxed advertisement at the top right showing a photograph of a service station forecourt with pumps under a canopy. The advertisement reads 2900 S. Claiborne Ave., New Orleans, La., On U.S. Number 90, Repairs, Washing, Greasing, Tire-Battery Service and Complete line of Standard Products, Tourist Information, with the names E. L. Marsalis and J. L. Wicker. The page header reads PLEASE MENTION THE GREEN BOOK.
caption: A service station on U.S. 90 in New Orleans, advertising in the 1941 edition. Count what one business is offering: fuel, repairs, a wash, and tourist information. That last item is the tell. Ordinary businesses were absorbing needs the road refused to meet, and the page header asks you to say where you found them.
credit: Staff of the Negro Motorist Green Book & its advertisers. The Negro Motorist Green Book 1941 - New Orleans 01.jpg. Public domain. Via Wikimedia Commons. https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:The_Negro_Motorist_Green_Book_1941_-_New_Orleans_01.jpg
